decisions.reason: Published September 30, within the frozen window. Useful new evidence for choosing a minimal experimental baseline: the authors compare harnesses with matched backbones, hardware and time, separating validation-based selection from hidden-test oracle selection ([saved §§3–4](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=3%20Experimental%20settings)). Attribute results to this preprint's authors; statistical indistinguishability does not establish equivalence or universal harness redundancy. Human researchers chose tasks, prompts, benchmark repairs and baseline configurations; the original29 and repaired30 evaluations must remain distinct ([saved A.1–A.2](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=A.1%20MLE-bench%20tasks%20used)). NatureBench permits repeated evaluation and reports oracle-best outcomes, so it is not equivalent to untouched final-test verification ([saved D.6](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=D.6%20NatureBench)). Cost estimates assume cache pricing and separate experiment hardware from inference hosting; minimal orchestration does not establish lower total cost ([saved A.4](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=A.4%20LLM%20backbones%20used)). The authors evaluate their own system and acknowledge tuning asymmetry, limited seeds and contamination risk; no independent replication or external researcher assessment is supplied ([saved G.1](data/assets/7f0901064878a294934bd154/6c598d9a3db4f487a0045a147e48bc3e4064e2b81bf388f4ac0947b9d96c78ec/text.txt#:~:text=G.1%20Limitations)). Student implication: compare a simple execution loop against added orchestration using fixed budgets and protected evaluation.

Published October 2, within the window; October 9 is an update, not a separate development. Accept for scrutiny of proposal evaluation and experiment planning, not evidence of successful autonomous execution: the authors explicitly stop systems before implementation, while the proposal schema requires baselines, ablations and falsifiable predictions ([saved §5.1](data/assets/7f93d63faaf11f733276a443/1c8d31d1a52853a33abbf82a2909b64babf8ea03d6714eb54e2df4ed7128e44a/text.txt#:~:text=5.1%20Experiment%20Setup), [saved A.2](data/assets/7f93d63faaf11f733276a443/1c8d31d1a52853a33abbf82a2909b64babf8ea03d6714eb54e2df4ed7128e44a/text.txt#:~:text=A.2%20Agent%20Output%20Schemas)). Disclose headline ambiguity: the abstract's roughly 15K papers include training data; only 277 are held-out tests. The reported 14.0% advantage is a 14.0-point subtraction, 74.6 minus 60.6, not a 14% relative improvement ([saved §4.2 and Table 1](data/assets/7f93d63faaf11f733276a443/1c8d31d1a52853a33abbf82a2909b64babf8ea03d6714eb54e2df4ed7128e44a/text.txt#:~:text=4.2%20Training%20data%20construction)). E.1 says tests were used only for final evaluation, whereas F.4 compares multiple checkpoint combinations on the full test split; the selection chronology needs clarification. Do not use unresolved results to establish superiority or cost savings ([saved E.1](data/assets/7f93d63faaf11f733276a443/1c8d31d1a52853a33abbf82a2909b64babf8ea03d6714eb54e2df4ed7128e44a/text.txt#:~:text=E.1%20Training%20and%20Inference%20Configuration), [saved F.4](data/assets/7f93d63faaf11f733276a443/1c8d31d1a52853a33abbf82a2909b64babf8ea03d6714eb54e2df4ed7128e44a/text.txt#:~:text=F.4%20Checkpoint%20Selection)). Training changes LoRA weights; it is not merely better prompting. Budgets are not matched across external systems, and training uses substantial H100 infrastructure (E.1). The authors' human and cross-judge checks are useful but remain within their own evaluation; require human review of same-family judge conclusions as a safeguard, without asserting demonstrated bias ([saved §5.4](data/assets/7f93d63faaf11f733276a443/1c8d31d1a52853a33abbf82a2909b64babf8ea03d6714eb54e2df4ed7128e44a/text.txt#:~:text=5.4%20Q3)). This is a developer-authored preprint with an interest in its own system's success, no supplied independent replication, and no supplied financial-conflict disclosure. Its concrete editorial value is teaching students to separate judged novelty from experimentally verified benefit.

Published October 1, within the window, but relevance fails. The procedure asks a chatbot to assess knowledge and create targeted flashcards; the demonstrated artifact is a 37-card puppy-training deck, not autonomous computational experimentation or verification. No controlled baseline, held-out learning assessment, execution logs or measured improvement supports the title's superiority claim ([saved procedure and demonstration](data/assets/810ca788d6580a6871563f4d/2ec6998b1c53899734b6cb244fefc18311d1635c79e90220c4b2743ae1235252/text.txt#:~:text=The%20fix)). It may be useful study advice, but artifact production does not demonstrate improved outcomes or a new research-automation capability. The author promotes a paid subscriber skill, creating a direct commercial interest; the paid implementation is not supplied for inspection ([saved commercial offer](data/assets/810ca788d6580a6871563f4d/2ec6998b1c53899734b6cb244fefc18311d1635c79e90220c4b2743ae1235252/text.txt#:~:text=Dig%20deeper)). Reject for scope and insufficient outcome evidence rather than defer for access to that peripheral product.

Published October 8, within the window. Useful new author-reported evidence on selecting experiments using historical records: the study compares record-conditioned predictions with no-history, kNN and ridge baselines and withholds target outcomes and near-duplicate intervention groups. The predictor's weights remain fixed; this is in-context conditioning, not model training ([saved §§2.2–3.2](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=2.2%20LLMs%20as%20Research%20World%20Models)). Preserve contrary results: cross-environment selection worsens on Marin, and kNN/ridge beat the record-conditioned model on inference-optimization regret despite its stronger global ranking. Prediction quality therefore does not guarantee better budget allocation ([saved Tables 4–5](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=3.3%20RWM%20Predictions%20Improve%20Experiment%20Selection)). Multi-round results use five evaluations of scheduled candidates with recorded outcomes and a budget beginning after initial history acquisition; they do not establish unrestricted autonomous discovery or end-to-end cost savings ([saved E.1–E.3](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=E.1%20Candidate%20sampling%20and%20arrivals)). Transfer evidence is limited to autoregressive pretraining, and some confidence intervals include zero ([saved D.1](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=D.1%20Uncertainty%20in%20cross-environment%20predictions)). Authors produced the records and reviewed AI-assisted work; this remains one research lineage with no supplied independent replication. Commercial API dependence limits reproducibility, release is prospective, and affiliations or financial conflicts are not established by the supplied text ([saved responsibility, ethics and reproducibility statements](data/assets/813b9149789f0913c5bfb94d/4e9fb103fdae9cf7e73a08394a425933da944a26fb69499d2c2935840571b3d8/text.txt#:~:text=AI%20use%20statement)). Student implication: retain failed experiments alongside successful ones, test forecasts against simple baselines, and verify selected interventions through real execution.
